subject: FieldOps site anchoring: node profiles, NVMe zoning and ephemeral PV policy
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: FieldOps site anchoring: node profiles, NVMe zoning and ephemeral PV policy

Hi team,

I started synthesizing the notes from yesterday's site call with Starchain. They want a concise plan we can hand to their infra team for the on-prem cluster footprint and the persistent/ephemeral storage guarantees. Key constraints from the call: single-rack per site initially, dual-10Gb uplinks to aggregation, and local NVMe per host (no shared SAN). They expect low-latency inference for cache-heavy workloads and are OK with ephemeral caches but NOT for model checkpoints.

Proposed high-level approach (draft):
- Node pools:
  - anchor-core: 3 x m48-like hosts (8x A100-class), reserved for model-serving Pods that must have stable local PVs for model artifacts and checkpoints. Taints: dedicated=true:NoSchedule.
  - anchor-burst: autoscaling pool (1-6 instances) for spiky batch/async work and non-persistent inferencing jobs; uses local NVMe for caches (ephemeral).
  - infra-small: 2-3 small nodes for control-plane-adjacent workloads (monitoring, logging, CSI).
- Storage classes and policies:
  - sc-checkpoint (replicated remote backup): PVs backed by NFS/S3 gateway to an on-prem object store — used for model checkpoints (async uploads to object store required by app).
  - sc-local-fast (ephemeral): local persistent volumes provisioned via Local PersistentVolumes + LocalPath Provisioner with explicit topology labels (rack/host). This class has no snapshot/backup by default; pods must tolerate data loss.
  - sc-ops (persistent): small PVs for logging/metrics with a lifecycle policy to drain to central object storage nightly.
- Eviction and failure handling:
  - Kubelet eviction thresholds tuned aggressively for anchor-core to avoid unnecessary OOM kills; kube-reserved and system-reserved configured.
  - PodDisruptionBudgets for serving replicas (minAvailable=2) and anti-affinity rules across hosts.

Questions we need answered from Starchain before we finalize:
1) Is losing NVMe-backed cache acceptable for up to 30s during host replacement? (their previous answers suggested yes for cache but NOT for checkpoints)
2) Do they have an on-prem S3-compatible object store we can use for sc-checkpoint remote copies?
3) Are we allowed to run a small replicated block store (rook/ceph) or do they forbid cluster storage services?

Next steps I propose: I'll draft a PV policy doc for their infra team (pv-policy-draft.md attached) and a one-page rack/node inventory template (site-inventory.xlsx). Can Dev and Laura review the node-pool sizing and the sc-checkpoint backup flow by Monday? I want this to be prescriptive enough that their infra team can provision resources without back-and-forth.

Thanks,
Rachel
Rachel Kim
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachments: site-inventory.xlsx (template), pv-policy-draft.md (draft storage class definitions)
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FieldOps site anchoring: node profiles, NVMe zoning and ephemeral PV policy

Thanks Rachel — good framing. A couple of quick notes from infra perspective after skimming the attachments:

- Node sizing: the anchor-core recommendation looks reasonable but call out the expected per-host GPU memory headroom (we should list expected model sizes + batch windows). I added a column in site-inventory.xlsx for model memory targets.
- Multi-tenancy: if this rack hosts non-Redwood workloads, we need stronger isolation. Suggest:
  - nodeAffinity + taints/tolerations as you noted,
  - runtimeClass for inference containers to pin CPU manager policy and isolate hugepages if needed.
- Local PVs: For sc-local-fast we should specify: local volume topology labels (topology.kubernetes.io/zone replaced with rack.local/hostname), and a pre-provisioning step in their provisioning playbook to create NodeLocal PersistentVolumes for each NVMe device. See pv-policy-draft.md where I commented on using the LocalPath provisioner vs static PVs.
- Checkpoints: if Starchain cannot provide an S3-compatible endpoint, we should offer an interim: a lightweight rsync-based periodic push from anchor-core to a designated backup host (same rack) that then ships to the remote site. Not ideal but acceptable for MVP.

I attached a quick markup in pv-policy-draft.md and updated the inventory template with model mem and expected checkpoint frequency.

Action items:
- Laura: can you craft the recommended kubelet eviction and kube-reserved snippet we want them to apply (should fit in a single copy-paste block)?
- Marissa: please draft a short note to include in the SOW clarifying which classes we consider non-backed and what SLAs mean for them.

If both are OK I will convert the draft into a short ops playbook we can hand them on the kickoff call.

Cheers,
Dev

Attachments: site-inventory.xlsx (updated), pv-policy-draft.md (Dev comments)
From: Samir Rao <samir@starchain.io>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@starchain.io
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FieldOps site anchoring: node profiles, NVMe zoning and ephemeral PV policy

Rachel — thanks for the clear plan. A couple of clarifications from our side after reviewing the attachments:

- Confirmed: the racks will not have a shared SAN. We can provide an on-prem S3-compatible endpoint but it will be throttled during business hours (we will share details later).
- NVMe guarantees: caches are fine to lose on host replacement but we need a documented restore path for model checkpoints. We'll accept sc-local-fast for cache and sc-checkpoint must have async copy to S3 within 5 minutes of write.
- We prefer NOT to run a complex distributed block store in the rack (no Ceph/rook).

Can you please update the pv-policy-draft.md with the async-copy requirement and an emergency restore checklist (how to redeploy from S3 and validate checksums)? Also include the runbook step that if an anchor-core node goes down we spin a replacement and force a model rehydrate from S3 within the same maintenance window.

I'll ask our infra lead to fill the model-memory column in the inventory template and return it by Wed EOD.

Samir Rao
Infra Lead, Starchain Inc.
